# Dev-gated in-page capture scene director

A dev-only page-side handle (`window.__aiHellCaptureDirector`) that switches the already-running page to a discovered gym scene by key, so one continuously-running `MediaRecorder` can span every scene of a multi-scene capture (AH-0MUX2NLFZ00128WC). Inert in production builds; mirrors the established `window.__aiHellScenario` dev-gated handle pattern (`src/core/devScenario.ts`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Covers parent AC2.** A dev-only page-side handle — e.g. `window.__aiHellCaptureDirector.start(key)` — starts a discovered, non-parameterised gym scene by key **inside the already-running page** (no navigation/reload), so one continuously-running `MediaRecorder` spans every scene. It is inert in production builds (`import.meta.env.DEV` gate; `npm run check-bundle` still passes) and rejects unknown/unsupported keys (including the parameterised `GymFodderEnemies` and `GymLevel`) with a clear error rather than silently doing nothing.
- **Key resolution pure.** A pure, unit-tested resolver accepts the discovered non-parameterised gym scene keys and rejects everything else.
- **Boot registration.** The handle is registered at boot (`src/core/boot.ts`) in dev builds only; unit tests cover both the key-validation logic and the dev gate.
- **No navigation.** Starting a scene neither navigates nor reloads the page; the game instance and the running recorder keep going.

## Key Files

- `src/core/captureDirector.ts` (new)
- `src/core/captureDirector.test.ts` (new)
- `src/core/devScenario.ts` (established dev-gated `window` handle pattern — mirror it)
- `src/core/runEndedSignal.ts` (dev-gated page↔capture signalling pattern)
- `src/core/boot.ts` (register in dev builds only)
- `src/utils/gymDiscovery.ts` (discovered gym scene keys)

## Minimal Implementation

1. `resolveSceneKey(key, discoveredKeys)`: pure validation — the key must be a discovered gym scene and in the watchable registry; reject `GymFodderEnemies`/`GymLevel` and unknown keys with a clear error.
2. `registerCaptureDirector(game)`: attach `window.__aiHellCaptureDirector = { start(key) { resolve…; game.scene.start(key); } }` gated by `import.meta.env.DEV`.
3. Register the call in `src/core/boot.ts` dev-only, mirroring the `devScenario` handle placement.
4. Hermetic unit tests for key validation + dev gate (no browser).
5. Verify `npm run check-bundle` still passes (no Node-only leakage into the production bundle).

## Dependencies

- The watchable-registry source of truth from the pure scene-capture module (sibling) — one shared list for CLI and director.

## Deliverables

- Dev-gated in-page scene switcher + hermetic unit tests + boot wiring; production bundle unaffected.
data.title: Dev-gated in-page capture scene director

# Test: wrapAware config plumbing

Test-first verification slice for the `wrapAware` parameter (parent AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8, AC1 + AC5). Pins the data-driven boolean's default, seed exclusions, CSV wiring and editor exposure **before** the implementation item lands, so the pipeline change is driven by failing tests.

## Goal

Pin the full config pipeline for `wrapAware`: default `true`, `march`/`centipede` seeded `false`, CSV persist + round-trip, editor-panel visibility.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A test asserts a generic archetype resolves `wrapAware === true` when the field is absent from its seed config.
- Tests assert the `march` and `centipede` seed configs carry `wrapAware === false` (the explicit exclusion list).
- A CSV round-trip test asserts a `wrapAware` column persists and reloads through the config CSV path; a missing/empty value falls back to `true`.
- A test asserts the field is enumerable through the existing `EnemyConfig` editor/config plumbing without extra per-field admin.
- All tests pass deterministically (no wall clock, no RNG).

## Key Files

- `src/core/configTypes.ts`
- `src/core/configDefaults.ts`
- `src/data/enemy-configs.csv`
- `src/core/enemyConfig.ts`
- `src/utils/csvEdit.ts`
data.title: Test: wrapAware config plumbing

# Data-driven force-field fields plus the pure resolver

**Parent:** AH-0MVJ8W4GE007OMNT (AC1).
**Depends on:** Resolver and codec contract tests (AH-0MVM8GQKI006B50M) (red contracts must exist first).

## Goal

As a balance engineer, I want per-archetype force-field strength to be
data-driven — which archetypes are shielded, from which level, and how the hit
count grows — so I can shape late-campaign difficulty from the CSV without
touching scene code.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Data-driven per-archetype fields.** New `EnemyConfig` fields `forceFieldStartLevel`, `forceFieldStartHits`, `forceFieldMaxHits` added to types, CSV codec, defaults and rows, with the pure resolver.
- `EnemyConfig` gains `forceFieldStartLevel` (campaign level at which the
  archetype first gains a field; `0` = never shielded),
  `forceFieldStartHits` (field hits when it appears) and `forceFieldMaxHits`
  (field hits at the campaign maximum level), each with JSDoc stating the
  neutral default — `0` / `1` / `1` — so **every existing enemy is unshielded
  at level 1** and the shipped campaign is behaviourally unchanged at L1.
- `src/core/csv.ts` numeric codec reads/writes the three columns; absent
  columns default to `0`/`1`/`1`; `src/core/configDefaults.ts` seeds the
  defaults; the CSV header comments document each column.
- `src/core/enemyForceField.ts` (**new**) exports a pure, Phaser-free
  `enemyForceFieldHits(level, config)` implementing
  `clamp(round(lerp(startHits @ startLevel → maxHits @ maxLevel)), 0, 5)`,
  documented with the formula and reusing `clampLevel` from the landed
  `src/core/levelScaling.ts` (AH-0MVLJEE7O008RX9X) for level clamping.
- Shipped CSV rows carry per-archetype values with **subtle curve variations**
  (Q5): heavier archetypes (Tank, Harvester) get higher `forceFieldStartHits`
  /`forceFieldMaxHits` than light ones; start levels vary per archetype
  (some L2, others L3+); no archetype is shielded at L1.
- The red contract tests from the sibling test item go green; existing
  `csv`/`config`/`configStore` suites stay green; persisted blobs still load.
- Resolver is deterministic: same level + config ⇒ identical value.

## Documented assumptions

- Field strength is a pure function of `(level, config)` — no RNG.
- The campaign maximum level is 10 (`DEFAULT_LEVEL_SCALING_MAX_LEVEL`).

## Key Files

- `src/core/configTypes.ts` — `EnemyConfig` fields.
- `src/core/configDefaults.ts`, `src/core/configStore.ts`,
  `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` — defaults, persisted-blob compatibility, rows.
- `src/core/csv.ts` — numeric codec + header comments.
- `src/core/enemyForceField.ts` — **new** resolver.
data.title: Force-field config and resolver

# TDD red phase: pin entity absorb/break and the ram rule

**Parent:** AH-0MVJ8W4GE007OMNT (AC2).
**Depends on:** Force-field config and resolver (AH-0MVM8GRQ8006HGPK) (needs the resolved hit count).
**Blocks:** Entity force-field layer (AH-0MVM8GUZG008AWSU).

## Goal

As a developer, I want the absorb-before-hull, break-once and ram-absorb
semantics pinned by tests before they are implemented, so every damage source
keeps routing through the single shared `takeDamage()` seam.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC2 — Force-field absorbs hits before the hull.** A shielded enemy survives its field hits first — pinned by contract tests before implementation.
- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.test.ts` pins:
  - an enemy built with `N` field hits exposes the remaining field hits;
  - `takeDamage()` while the field is up decrements the field and leaves
    `health` **unchanged**, reporting the hit as absorbed (distinct from a hull
    hit) so scenes can give different feedback;
  - the break (field reaching 0) is signalled **exactly once** and never again;
  - after the break the next hit decrements `health` as today — the 1-HP
    majority dies on that hit, the 5-HP Harvester still needs 5;
  - an enemy constructed with **no** field hits behaves exactly as before
    (backwards-compatible default), and `health` is still the only thing a ram
    or bullet touches for unshielded enemies.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.test.ts` pins the ram rule (Q6 = B): ramming a
  **shielded** enemy consumes exactly one field hit, destroys **neither** side
  and does not call `onPlayerHit`/`_hitPlayer`; ramming an **unshielded** enemy
  keeps today's both-destroyed behaviour; a second ram inside the re-arm window
  consumes nothing; Thorn Field keeps precedence and its own cue.
- `src/entities/enemyFactory.test.ts` pins that the effective field hit count
  is threaded from config into the constructed entity.
- Tests demonstrably fail before the implementation item lands (record the red
  run in a comment).

## Key Files

- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.test.ts`, `src/entities/Harvester.test.ts`.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.test.ts` — ram-absorb contract.
- `src/entities/enemyFactory.test.ts` — threading contract.
data.title: Entity field and ram contract tests
